contentHtml:
Tambaque Spring (Nacimiento de Tambaque) is a turquoise spring in the municipality of Aquismón, San Luis Potosí, less than 60 minutes from Ciudad Valles. Aquismón is part of the Huasteca Potosina, a region with some of the most varied natural scenery in central Mexico, from canyons and caves to rivers and crystal-clear springs that flow straight out of the limestone mountains. Aquismón has become one of the most visited municipalities in the Huasteca Potosina thanks to attractions like the Sótano de las Golondrinas (Cave of the Swallows) and Tambaque Spring itself. Every year, thousands of travelers head to this spot looking for Tambaque without knowing exactly how much entry costs, whether it's open, or which road to take without getting lost in the Huasteca mountains. That uncertainty before the trip is real, and this guide is here to clear it up.

In this article you'll find everything you need to plan your visit to Tambaque in Aquismón in 2026: updated prices, detailed routes, which tours run in the area, and the months when the Huasteca's turquoise water is at its most spectacular. In 2026, individual admission costs just $10 MXN per person, which makes it one of the cheapest entry fees in the whole region.

At www.huasteca-potosina.com we work with local guides and operators in the region. This guide is updated with real experiences from people who travel the Huasteca Potosina every week. Last updated: September 2026. If you'd rather leave the logistics to experts, check out our all-inclusive packages with a hotel in Xilitla.

Tambaque Spring in Aquismón: what it is and why it's worth the trip

What exactly is Tambaque Spring, and where is it?

Tambaque Spring is a natural spring that flows straight out of the limestone mountains in the municipality of Aquismón, forming a natural pool of turquoise water that stays very cold all year. The site belongs to the community of Tambaque and is run by a local ejido committee (the community's land-management body), which regulates access. According to the local guides we coordinate through this site, the water stays between emerald green and turquoise blue even in the rainy season, thanks to the type of limestone that filters the groundwater.

Visitors agree that the walk in — a short trail among wild tamarind trees — is part of the experience before you even see the water. The contrast between the tropical vegetation and the mirror of crystal-clear water is what sets this place apart from other swimming spots in the region. The Tamul Expedition and Rafting on the Tampaón River run near Tambaque if you want to add another day of touring.

The Tanchanaco Package: the best option for families

The Tanchanaco Package (Paquete Tanchanaco) combines entry to Tambaque Spring with La Garita for $50 MXN per person, and includes parking, changing rooms, showers and restrooms. For families with kids or groups of more than four, this rate is the best value for money in the area in 2026. You buy the package right at the site entrance, no reservation needed, and the site is open every day from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.. In high season, try to arrive before 10:00 a.m. to get a spot in the parking lot, which holds about 40 vehicles.

If you're going to combine this visit with other natural attractions in the mountains, we recommend reading our guide to Huichihuayán Spring (Nacimiento de Huichihuayán), another spring with similar features a little over an hour away. Planning both visits for the same weekend is completely doable from Ciudad Valles.

Prices, hours and how to plan your visit to Tambaque in 2026

How much does it cost to visit Tambaque Spring in 2026?

The most basic price at Tambaque in 2026 is $10 MXN per person for admission, plus $30 MXN for parking and an extra $10 MXN if you use the restrooms. All in, a visit for one person can cost as little as $50 MXN if you arrive in your own car.

July and August are the busiest weeks of the year at Tambaque. If you're looking for a quieter visit, October and November have water that's just as clear with much less traffic. See available tours in the Huasteca Potosina to compare options with transportation included.

Opening hours, and confirming before you go

The site is open every day from 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., but it's a good idea to confirm it's open before you leave. The ejido committee that runs the site may close it on local holidays, for maintenance or for community events without notice in outside media. The practical advice is to contact the community through its official Facebook page before leaving Ciudad Valles, especially on a long weekend or during vacation season. If you plan to visit in October, also read our guide to the weather in the Huasteca Potosina in October to know what conditions to expect.

Practical tips before visiting Tambaque Spring

Preparing well for your trip to Tambaque Spring makes the difference between a perfect day and one full of surprises. These are the issues we most often help the travelers we coordinate with, based on real visits in 2025 and 2026.

  • Confirm it's open the day before: Message the site's committee on Facebook before you leave. Showing up to an unannounced closure is the most common mistake independent visitors make.
  • Bring cash in small bills: Admission ($10 MXN), parking ($30 MXN) and restrooms ($10 MXN) are paid in cash. There are no card terminals at the site or in the nearby community.
  • Combine it with other waterfalls in the area: The route from Ciudad Valles lets you visit Tambaque in Aquismón and then continue on to the Minas Viejas Waterfalls (Cascadas de Minas Viejas) or the Siete Cascadas de Tamasopo on the same day if you leave early.
  • The right clothes and gear: Wear water sandals or water shoes with good grip. The tamarind trail can be wet and slippery. Bring biodegradable sunscreen, since regular sunscreen is banned at the ejido-run springs in the mountains. See our packing checklist for the Potosí jungle.
  • Realistic minimum budget per person: If you drive your own car and use the Tanchanaco Package, spending at the site won't go over $50 MXN. Add gas from Ciudad Valles (about $150–200 MXN round trip) and food in the area (local fondas, or small family eateries, from $80 MXN a plate). A full day at Tambaque Spring can cost less than $400 MXN per person if you travel as a group.

How do you get to Tambaque Spring from Ciudad Valles?

The route from Ciudad Valles to Tambaque Spring is one of the most direct in the whole Huasteca Potosina for a natural attraction of this caliber. The drive takes less than an hour, so it works even if you only have half a day. Knowing the route in detail avoids the most common mix-up: many travelers think they have to go through the town of Aquismón, when there's actually a faster, direct turnoff.

Detailed route: Highway 85 south to Tambaque

From Ciudad Valles, take federal Highway 85 south for about 55 km. When you reach the junction known as "San Pedro de las Anonas," turn toward Tambaque following the local signs. You don't need to go through the town of Aquismón, which saves you 15 to 20 minutes. The road is paved all the way to the site. Check out guided tours in the area if you'd rather not drive the rest of your trip.

Transportation options: your own car or a colectivo

If you don't have your own vehicle, colectivos (shared vans) from Ciudad Valles to Aquismón leave regularly from the bus station, but they don't stop right at the site: you'll need to get off at the junction and walk or hire a local mototaxi. Frequently asked questions about Tambaque Spring

Can you swim in Tambaque Spring all year?

Yes, you can swim at Tambaque Spring all year. The water comes from an underground aquifer and is very cold, so ease in slowly to avoid the shock. In the rainy season (June–September) the flow increases and the color can turn greener; the clearest turquoise water is between November and May 2026.

How much is admission to Tambaque in 2026?

Individual admission at Tambaque is $10 MXN per person. Parking costs $30 MXN and the restrooms another $10 MXN. The Tanchanaco Package, which includes entry to Tambaque plus La Garita, changing rooms and showers, costs $50 MXN per person. Everything is paid in cash.

How long is the drive from Ciudad Valles to Tambaque Spring?

The trip is about 55 km on Highway 85 south, with a driving time of under 60 minutes in normal conditions. You turn off directly at the San Pedro de las Anonas junction, with no need to go through the town of Aquismón. The road is paved the whole way.

Is Tambaque in Aquismón safe for young kids or couples?

Tambaque Spring is a good fit for families with kids and for couples. The water access area has shallow spots near the edge. There's almost no current, but the water is very cold and the bottom is slippery, so keep an eye on the kids. Bring life jackets for children under 8 and water shoes with good grip for the whole family. The site has restrooms and a shaded area to rest.

What else can I visit near Tambaque Spring on the same day?

Tambaque Spring's location makes it easy to combine with other attractions in the Huasteca mountains. If you leave Ciudad Valles early, you can get to Tambaque in the morning and continue in the afternoon to the Minas Viejas Waterfalls, which are on the other side of Ciudad Valles, 1 h 45 min from the city, or to Huichihuayán Spring, a little over an hour away. If you'd prefer a planned route with set times and stops, our full-day tours of the Huasteca Potosina don't go into Tambaque, but these run in the same area: the Tamul Expedition and Rafting on the Tampaón River.

Is there food service at Tambaque Spring?

There's no formal restaurant on site, but at the entrance and around the community of Tambaque there are stands and local fondas serving typical Huastec dishes such as zacahuil (a giant tamale slow-cooked in a wood-fired oven), bocoles (thick little corn cakes with fillings) and enchiladas potosinas (San Luis Potosí-style enchiladas), with prices starting at $60 MXN a plate. Bring your own water and snacks for your time in the water, since there are no stores inside the natural area. If you're visiting on an organized tour, ask your operator whether food is included or handled separately along the route.
